title: Osteoarthritis of the knee, hip and hand
subject: rheumatology-dermatology
summary: Core care for every patient is education, exercise and weight loss (5% or more if overweight); add a topical NSAID (knee, hand), then an oral NSAID at the lowest dose with gastroprotection, and intra-articular glucocorticoid for knee or hip flares. Avoid routine opioids, glucosamine, hyaluronic acid and PRP.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Clinical diagnosis without imaging (NICE NG226): age 45 or over, activity-related joint pain, and no morning stiffness or stiffness lasting 30 minutes or less.

Knee: crepitus, bony enlargement, reduced flexion. Hip: groin or anterior thigh pain with painful, reduced internal rotation. Hand: Heberden (DIP) and Bouchard (PIP) nodes, thumb-base (first CMC) pain.

Atypical features suggest another or additional diagnosis: prolonged morning stiffness, rapid progression, a hot swollen joint, young age, rest or night pain, weight loss or fever. Consider inflammatory arthritis, gout or CPPD, septic arthritis, avascular necrosis, malignancy, or pain referred from the spine or hip.
Erosive hand OA: painful, inflamed interphalangeal joints with central erosions on X-ray; can mimic inflammatory arthritis.

sections.title: Investigations
items: Do not routinely image to diagnose OA. X-ray (weight-bearing for the knee) for atypical features, diagnostic doubt or before surgical referral; radiographic severity correlates poorly with symptoms.
Blood tests are not needed in typical OA; check ESR or CRP, RF or anti-CCP, and urate if inflammatory arthritis or gout is suspected. Aspirate an effusion if infection or crystals are possible.
Before an oral NSAID: renal function, blood pressure, cardiovascular and GI bleeding risk, and anticoagulant or antiplatelet use.

sections.title: Core non-drug care (all patients)
items: Education and self-management; explain that activity does not wear out the joint. Refer to physiotherapy or occupational therapy when function is limited.
Exercise is strongly recommended for knee and hip OA (strengthening, aerobic, aquatic; tai chi, and yoga for the knee); hand exercises for hand OA (ACR 2026).
Weight loss is strongly recommended for knee and hip OA with overweight or obesity; benefit starts at about 5% of body weight and increases with more.
GLP-1 receptor agonist (for example semaglutide) with diet and exercise is conditionally recommended for knee OA with obesity (ACR 2026).

Adjuncts: walking stick in the opposite hand, knee braces, thumb-base orthoses, taping, local heat or cold, CBT, acupuncture and massage. Lateral or medial wedged insoles and TENS are not recommended.

sections.title: Drug treatment
items: Topical NSAID first for knee and hand OA (strong) and preferred over oral NSAIDs, especially in older people and those with comorbidity.

Oral NSAID (strong) at the lowest effective dose for the shortest time, intermittently if possible, with a PPI if GI risk. OARSI: with GI risk use a COX-2 inhibitor or NSAID plus PPI; avoid all oral NSAIDs with cardiovascular disease or frailty. Avoid in eGFR below 30 and heart failure.

Intra-articular glucocorticoid for knee or hip OA (strong), ultrasound-guided for the hip; conditionally for hand OA. Relief lasts weeks; use for flares or to enable exercise, generally no more often than every 3 months.

When NSAIDs are unsuitable: duloxetine (conditional), topical capsaicin for knee OA (conditional), paracetamol (conditional, modest benefit, ACR 2026). OARSI and NICE advise against routine paracetamol; NICE allows it only for infrequent short-term use.
Opioids are conditionally not recommended (ACR 2026) and OARSI strongly advises against oral and transdermal opioids; NICE: do not offer strong opioids.
Erosive hand OA: methotrexate is now conditionally recommended (ACR 2026); it is not recommended for knee or hip OA.

sections.title: Review and referral
items: Review pain, function, weight, exercise adherence and drug adverse effects regularly.

Refer for joint replacement assessment when symptoms substantially affect quality of life and non-surgical care has failed or is unsuitable; do not use age, BMI, smoking or radiographic grade alone to deny referral (NICE).
Genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation is conditionally recommended for knee OA refractory to other care (ACR 2026).
Arthroscopic lavage or debridement is not recommended unless there is true mechanical locking (NICE).

sections.title: Not recommended and pitfalls
items: Strongly not recommended (ACR 2026): glucosamine, chondroitin and their combinations, hydroxychloroquine, bisphosphonates, TNF inhibitors, PRP and stem cell injections.
Conditionally not recommended: intra-articular hyaluronic acid, botulinum toxin, dextrose prolotherapy, colchicine, vitamin D, fish oil, pregabalin, gabapentin and tricyclics.
Long-term oral NSAIDs without renal, BP and GI review, especially with an ACE inhibitor or ARB plus a diuretic (AKI risk).
Missing septic arthritis or gout in an acutely hot, swollen OA joint.
Ordering MRI for typical knee OA; it rarely changes management.

drugs.name: Diclofenac 1% gel (topical)
drugs.dose: Apply 2 to 4 g to the affected joint 3 to 4 times daily
drugs.notes: First line for knee and hand OA; low systemic absorption.

drugs.name: Naproxen
drugs.dose: 250 to 500 mg orally twice daily with food (maximum 1 g/day)
drugs.notes: Add a PPI if GI risk. Avoid in eGFR below 30, heart failure, cardiovascular disease and frailty.

drugs.name: Celecoxib
drugs.dose: 100 mg orally twice daily or 200 mg once daily
drugs.notes: COX-2 inhibitor for GI risk; same cardiovascular and renal cautions.

drugs.name: Triamcinolone acetonide (intra-articular)
drugs.dose: 40 mg into the knee or hip (hip under ultrasound guidance); smaller doses for hand joints
drugs.notes: Exclude infection first; generally no more often than every 3 months.

drugs.name: Duloxetine
drugs.dose: 30 mg orally once daily for 1 week, then 60 mg once daily
drugs.notes: Conditional option; nausea, dizziness; caution with other serotonergic drugs.

drugs.name: Capsaicin 0.025% cream
drugs.dose: Apply to the knee up to 4 times daily
drugs.notes: Knee OA only; burning early in treatment; wash hands after use.

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.dose: 500 mg to 1 g orally up to 4 times daily; maximum 4 g/day
drugs.notes: Lower maximum if weight under 50 kg, hepatic impairment or alcohol excess. Modest benefit; not for routine long-term use (NICE, OARSI).
